name: file-upload
title: File Upload
summary: Pick files by dropping them on a zone or choosing them from the system dialog.
description: Pick files by dropping them on a zone or by choosing them from the system dialog. The drop zone is the empty state's block (icon tile, title, hint) inside a dashed frame; every picked file is a tag (a file glyph, the name, a remove button) with its size beside it, and a refused file is a red tag with the reason. Behaviour by Ark UI's file-upload (Zag): limits on count, size and type. Controlled or uncontrolled.

anatomy.description: Ark's file-upload root: a column (label, drop zone, files), 8px apart. As wide as its container. data-dragging while files are dragged over it, data-disabled.
Visible name (the label prop): text.sm, medium, ink, the slider's and the field's label. It wraps, never truncates.

Ark's drop zone: role=button, focusable (the shared focus ring), radius card, a 1px dashed line-strong frame on the surface. A click, Enter or Space opens the system file dialog; files dropped on it are added. Holds the real EmptyState (size block): the upload-simple glyph in its tile, the title and the hint. Hovered by a mouse: color.hover; pressed: color.hover-2; while files are dragged over it: an accent frame on accent-tint. Disabled: half opacity, inert.
Ark's hidden file input, carrying the files for a form (name).
A list of files, one per line, 6px apart: the accepted files, then (Ark's rejected group) the refused ones. Each is absent when it has none.

One file: the tag, then its size (text.xs, tabular figures, ink-2, never wrapped) at the end of the line, or for a refused file the reason in red. Keyed by the file itself, never by its position, so removing a file leaves the others in place.

The real Tag (md, rounded, removable, with the file glyph as its icon), marked data-file-upload="file": the file's name, cut at the end with a title when the line is too narrow. Its remove button is named "Remove <name>" and removes the file. A refused file's tag is tone red.
The file's size (1.2 MB) or, for a refused file, why it was refused (Too large, Not an accepted type, Too many files…) in red.

items.type: File | { name: string, size: number, type?: string }

files.description: The accepted files. Controlled: files with onFilesChange. Uncontrolled: defaultFiles. A plain { name, size, type } stands for a file (an upload already on the server, a fixture).

label.description: Visible label above the drop zone.

hint.description: The drop zone's hint (what is accepted, the limits).

accept.description: Accepted types: MIME types (image/png, image/*) or extensions (.pdf). Anything else is refused.

maxFiles.description: How many files it takes; more are refused (Too many files).

maxFileSize.description: Largest file in bytes; larger ones are refused (Too large).

disabled.description: Inert at half opacity; the drop zone leaves the tab order.

events.filesChange: (files: File[]) the accepted files after a pick, a drop or a removal
events.reject: (rejections: { file: File, errors: string[] }[]) files that were refused

keyboard: Tab reaches the drop zone, then each file's remove button
Enter or Space on the drop zone opens the system file dialog
Enter or Space on a remove button removes that file
notes: The drop zone is role=button named by its title and hint; the label names the hidden input.
Each remove button is named "Remove <file name>".
A refused file stays in the list, in red with its reason, until it is removed, so the reason can be read.

motion: drop zone: background and frame colour over duration.fast (hover, press, files dragged over it), colour only

files: a file added after the first paint makes its room as it fades in: its line opens from 0fr to 1fr over duration.reveal, easing.out-strong (the collapsible's reveal), while its opacity rises over duration.base, so what is below slides down instead of jumping; files present at first paint do not move, and removing a file never makes the others enter again
remove buttons: the tag's own (the Button's press)
